ordered_diagnoses: Trigeminal Nerve Invasion by Malignant Melanoma

facts.raw_span: recurring forehead lesion, first excised 6 years prior to presentation
left proptosis and resistance to globe retropulsion with edema, erythema, and ptosis of the left upper eyelid
Adduction was limited on the left, with associated strabismus and forehead anesthesia in the V1 division of the trigeminal nerve
Left superior orbit mass extending along the supraorbital nerve to the cavernous sinus, with indistinct borders and fat stranding
Intense enhancement of the V1 branch of the left frontal nerve with associated fat stranding

concepts.why: The patient has a history of a recurring forehead lesion with a Breslow thickness of 6 mm, 14 mitotic figures/mm2, and extensive perineural and intraneural invasion, which are all characteristic of malignant melanoma.
The patient's symptoms, including forehead anesthesia in the V1 division of the trigeminal nerve and limited adduction on the left, are consistent with perineural invasion by malignant melanoma.
The patient's left proptosis, resistance to globe retropulsion, and associated strabismus are consistent with an orbital metastasis of malignant melanoma.
